He was the team's third leading scorer – averaging 10.1 points per game – for the fourth-place Australians.{{Cite web |url=http://www.fiba.com/pages/eng/fe/09/u19men/player/p/pid/75872/sid/4034/tid/239/accumulated-statistics.html |title=Matthew Dellavedova - Player Profile |website=FIBA.com |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171201132508/http://www.fiba.basketball/pages/eng/fe/09/u19men/player/p/pid/75872/sid/4034/tid/239/accumulated-statistics.html |archive-date=1 December 2017}} He was named in the [[Australia men's national basketball team|Australian senior national team]], the Boomers, to compete for the first time at the [[2009 FIBA Oceania Championship]]. At age 19, he was the youngest Australian player at the competition. He went on to compete for the Boomers at the [[Basketball at the 2012 Summer Olympics|2012 London Olympics]], the [[2014 FIBA Basketball World Cup|2014 World Cup]] in Spain, the [[Basketball at the 2016 Summer Olympics|2016 Rio Olympics]], and the [[2019 FIBA Basketball World Cup|2019 World Cup]] in China.
